\chapter{Communication Complexity — Det Rectangle}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.DeterministicCC.DetRectangle
\section{Overview}

This module establishes that every deterministic communication protocol induces a
monochromatic rectangle partition of the input space $X \times Y$ into at most
$2^c$ rectangles, where $c$ is the protocol's communication complexity.
It also derives the fooling-set lower-bound method, showing that the size of any
fooling set bounds $\mathrm{CC}(g)$ from below via $\lceil \log_2 |S| \rceil \leq \mathrm{CC}(g)$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Swap of a protocol input set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\leanok
Given a set $R \subseteq X \times Y$, $\texttt{swapInputSet}(R)$ is the set
$\{(y, x) \mid (x, y) \in R\} \subseteq Y \times X$ obtained by swapping the two
coordinates of every element.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in swapped set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_swapInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_swapInputSet}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\difficulty{1}
For any set $R \subseteq X \times Y$ and pair $(y, x) \in Y \times X$,
$(y, x) \in \texttt{swapInputSet}(R)$ if and only if $(x, y) \in R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Swap is an involution]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_swapInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_swapInputSet}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\difficulty{1}
For any set $R \subseteq X \times Y$, applying $\texttt{swapInputSet}$ twice recovers
$R$: $\texttt{swapInputSet}(\texttt{swapInputSet}(R)) = R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Preimage of a protocol input set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet}
\leanok
Given maps $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ and a set $R \subseteq X \times Y$,
$\texttt{preimageInputSet}(f_X, f_Y, R)$ is the set
$\{(x', y') \in X' \times Y' \mid (f_X(x'), f_Y(y')) \in R\}$, the pullback of $R$ along
the product map $f_X \times f_Y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in preimage input set]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_preimageInputSet}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_preimageInputSet}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet}
\difficulty{1}
For maps $f_X : X' \to X$, $f_Y : Y' \to Y$, a set $R \subseteq X \times Y$, and a pair
$(x', y') \in X' \times Y'$, we have $(x', y') \in \texttt{preimageInputSet}(f_X, f_Y, R)$
if and only if $(f_X(x'), f_Y(y')) \in R$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Auxiliary leaf rectangles relative to a constraint]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol}
For a protocol $p$ and sets $A \subseteq X$, $B \subseteq Y$, $\texttt{leafRectanglesAux}(p, A, B)$
is the collection of rectangles induced by the leaves of $p$ when the reachable inputs are
constrained to $A \times B$. It is defined by structural recursion: an output node yields
$\{A \times B\}$, while Alice (resp.\ Bob) nodes split $A$ (resp.\ $B$) according to the
branching function and recurse.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Protocol leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux}
The \emph{leaf rectangles} of a protocol $p : \texttt{Protocol}\,X\,Y\,\alpha$ form the
collection $\texttt{leafRectangles}(p) = \texttt{leafRectanglesAux}(p, X, Y)$, i.e.\ the set
of input rectangles induced by the leaves of $p$ over the full input space $X \times Y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Swap sends leaf rectangles to leaf rectangles (auxiliary)]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_swap}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_swap}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_cover, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swap, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet}
\difficulty{4}
If $R \in \texttt{leafRectanglesAux}(p, A, B)$, then
$\texttt{swapInputSet}(R) \in \texttt{leafRectanglesAux}(p.\texttt{swap}, B, A)$.
This is an internal auxiliary result proved by structural induction on the protocol.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Swap sends leaf rectangles to leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectangles_swap}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectangles_swap}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swap, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.swapInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_swap}
\difficulty{1}

\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet_mem_leafRectanglesAux_comap}

\begin{theorem}[Preimage sends leaf rectangles to leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.preimageInputSet_mem_leafRectangles_comap}

\leanok

\begin{lemma}[Auxiliary leaf rectangles are rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.aux_isRectangle}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.aux_isRectangle}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesAux, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle}
\difficulty{3}
Every element of $\texttt{leafRectanglesAux}(p, A, B)$ is a combinatorial rectangle, i.e.\
a set of the form $A' \times B'$ for some $A' \subseteq X$, $B' \subseteq Y$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Every protocol leaf rectangle is a rectangle]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isRectangle}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isRectangle}

\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Leaf rectangles form a monochromatic partition]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isMonoPartition}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isMonoPartition}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
If $p$ computes $g : X \to Y \to \alpha$, then the collection $\texttt{leafRectangles}(p)$

\begin{theorem}[Low complexity implies monochromatic partition with few parts]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.mono_partition_of_communicationComplexity_le}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.mono_partition_of_communicationComplexity_le}

If $\mathrm{CC}(g) \leq n$, then there exists a monochromatic rectangle partition of

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rectangle partition lower bound]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.le_communicationComplexity_of_forall_lt_ncard}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.le_communicationComplexity_of_forall_lt_ncard}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_iff, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.le_communicationComplexity_iff, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.mono_partition_of_communicationComplexity_le, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsMonoPartition}
\difficulty{4}
To prove $\mathrm{CC}(g) \geq n + 1$, it suffices to show that every monochromatic
rectangle partition of $g$ has more than $2^n$ parts: if every $\texttt{IsMonoPartition}\,P\,g$
satisfies $2^n < |P|$, then $(n+1) \leq \mathrm{CC}(g)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fooling set size bounded by $2^n$ when $\mathrm{CC}(g) \leq n$]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.foolingSet_ncard_le_pow_of_communicationComplexity_le}

\begin{theorem}[Fooling-set lower bound]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.clog_ncard_le_communicationComplexity}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.clog_ncard_le_communicationComplexity}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.foolingSet_ncard_le_pow_of_communicationComplexity_le, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsFoolingSet}
